data.title: Create a lightweight distant cloud layer
data.summary: Four licensed cloud alpha images and a fixed distant sky band. An LLM-assisted recipe with a concrete practice case, visual procedure and review gates.

facts.text: Principled BSDF combines surface layers with configurable material parameters.

prerequisites: An authorized Blender Geometry Nodes environment and a recorded tool version. Blender-specific references here are pinned to the 4.5 manual; check differences in your installed version.
Practice inputs: Four licensed cloud alpha images and a fixed distant sky band.

Permission to use the source assets and a writable derived-output location. Use a disposable project copy for edits. An MCP connection is optional; reviewed scripts or manual tool actions can follow the same procedure.
steps: Inspect the existing project, asset registry and target runtime for an equivalent cloud cards workflow. Reuse the closest source and preserve its original files.

Give Claude Code, Codex or another authorized coding assistant this practice brief: Four licensed cloud alpha images and a fixed distant sky band. Ask for a small plan and parameter/script diff; verify names and APIs against the installed tool version before applying it.
Place camera-facing cards beyond the playable scene with depth ordering
Use an alpha-compatible material and test against both dark and bright backgrounds
Compare overdraw with fewer larger cards and a static sky alternative

Save the derived candidate separately, record software versions and source/output identities, then perform the acceptance checks. Keep unresolved quality, performance and rights questions in the receipt.
data.output: A versioned create a lightweight distant cloud layer candidate, the input/parameter table, source identity and a review receipt with the checks below.
validation: Card edges do not reveal black fringes
Camera movement does not expose obvious side-on planes in the allowed view
Record actual observations separately from expected results; missing tests remain unrun.
limitations: Cards are a distant visual approximation, not volumetric weather.
Sintra-authored proposal, not an executed Blender/engine/solver test. The diagram illustrates the procedure and is not a render or execution receipt.
Cloud chat cannot directly control a local 3D app without an appropriate authorized bridge. Tool access, model availability, paid services and rendering resources must be checked separately.
tips: Keep clouds out of close fly-through paths unless you use a volume approach.
Let the LLM draft and explain bounded changes; use deterministic software to measure geometry, calculate trajectories and validate files.

data.prompt: Help me create a lightweight distant cloud layer in [existing authorized project]. First find an equivalent asset/workflow and inspect the installed tool version. Practice brief: Four licensed cloud alpha images and a fixed distant sky band. Propose the smallest parameter or script diff and explain each tool action. Follow the linked procedure, preserve original assets and stop on missing inputs or unsupported APIs. Check: Card edges do not reveal black fringes; Camera movement does not expose obvious side-on planes in the allowed view. Return actual observations, source/output identities and blockers. Do not call expected results completed tests or publish private source paths.
